title: Apple CEO Considers Chinese Memory Amid Shortage
key_facts: John Ternus, Apple's CEO since 1 September (succeeding Tim Cook, now executive chairman), told Time magazine in an interview published 15 Oct that memory supply constraints are 'clearly a serious crisis' and that Apple must 'review all options'.
He did not name Chinese firms; Chosun Ilbo reads the remark as not ruling out Chinese-made memory.
The Financial Times reported in July and the Wall Street Journal in August that Apple is testing DRAM from China's CXMT; no adoption or mass-production deal is finalised.

Seven US senators, including Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer, wrote to Apple on 29 July asking it not to use CXMT or YMTC chips; both are on the US Defense Department's list of Chinese military-linked companies.
Ternus said he has discussed the issue with Trump administration officials.
Industry sources say Samsung and SK Hynix raised low-power DRAM prices for iPhones in Q1 by 80% and 100% versus the prior quarter.
quote_evidence: "Memory supply constraints are clearly a serious crisis," adding, "It is our basic stance that we must review all options."
However, no actual product adoption or mass production agreements have been finalized.
why_it_matters_hint: A shift by Apple could weaken the pricing power of Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron, but it faces US political pressure.
